name: Ken Rosewall
milestone_by_age_26: Won the 1953 Australian Championships singles title at age 18, becoming the youngest champion in the tournament's history—a record that still stands; also won the 1953 French Championships and multiple doubles Grand Slam titles that year.
early_history_summary: Ken Rosewall started playing tennis at age 3 with a shortened racket on clay courts his father purchased. He played his first tournament at age 9 and won the Australian Hardcourt Championships under-14 title at age 11. Mentored by legendary coach Harry Hopman, he was part of the dominant Australian tennis ecosystem alongside rival and doubles partner Lew Hoad.
family_context_summary: Born to a middle-class family in Hurstville, Sydney; father Robert was a grocer who bought three clay tennis courts when Ken was one year old.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father Robert Rosewall played tennis and taught Ken from age 3, converting him from a natural left-hander to right-handed play.
primary_early_advantage_tags: father-coached, home tennis courts, Harry Hopman mentorship, Australian tennis ecosystem, early start age 3
evidence_summary: Ken Rosewall started playing tennis at age 3 on clay courts his father purchased, converted from a natural left-hander to right-handed by his father. He played his first tournament at age 9 and won the Australian Hardcourt Championships under-14 title at age 11. By 18, he won the 1953 Australian Championships, becoming the youngest champion in the tournament's history—a record that still stands. He was mentored by legendary Australian coach Harry Hopman and was part of the dominant Australian tennis ecosystem alongside rival and doubles partner Lew Hoad.
starting_point: Born to a middle-class family in Hurstville, Sydney; father Robert was a grocer who bought three clay tennis courts when Ken was one year old.
current_position: Retired tennis legend with 8 Grand Slam singles titles and 18 total major titles; considered one of the greatest tennis players of all time; resides in Australia.

name: Mark Hunt
milestone_by_age_26: Won the K-1 Oceania Tournament in February 2000 at age 25, qualifying for the K-1 World Grand Prix with a 15-4 professional kickboxing record.
early_history_summary: Mark Hunt grew up in a large Samoan family in South Auckland with a troubled youth that included two jail terms for violent offending. His fighting career began when a nightclub bouncer noticed his natural knockout power during a street altercation and invited him to train. With minimal formal training, Hunt won his first muay Thai fight and built a 15-4 kickboxing record by early 2000.

name: Jiang Jialiang
